subject: USAGE clause
notes: ALL THREE OBLIGATIONS MEASURED ON THE BYTES, NOT INFERRED. (1) "a radix of 2 is used to represent a numeric item" plus "the representation of any algebraic sign" - probe q2 (--std 2023) puts 258, -1 and 66051 into `PIC S9(4) BINARY` / `PIC S9(9) BINARY` leaves inside groups and reads each group's image byte by byte with FUNCTION ORD: 0x01 0x02, 0xFF 0xFF and 0x00 0x01 0x02 0x03 - two's complement, MOST SIGNIFICANT BYTE FIRST, the sign carried by the two's-complement encoding with no separate sign byte. Probe q3 adds the SCALED axis: `PIC S9(5)V99 BINARY` holding 12345.67 images as 0x00 0x12 0xD6 0x87 = 1234567, i.e. the UNSCALED value, and the implied point occupies no storage. (2) "Sufficient computer storage shall be allocated by the implementor to contain the maximum range of values implied by the associated decimal picture character-string" - this is the clause an implementor most easily fails, and it is the one PicInfo.StorageWidth is written against: probe q1 reports FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH 1/2/4/8/16 for S9(2)/S9(4)/S9(9)/S9(18)/S9(31), and the boundary is derived rather than conventional (a signed 18-digit max 10^18-1 fits 2^63-1, a signed 19-digit does not, so 19..38 digits take 16 bytes - the property's own comment says so). The floor was exercised at the top: `MOVE 9999999999999999999999999999999 TO` a `PIC S9(31) BINARY` and its negation both store and display exactly, and `PIC 9(31) BINARY` (unsigned) reports the same 16 - sign-independent, the GR12 precedent, documented. Scale keys on DIGITS not positions: `PIC S9(3)PPP BINARY` is 2 bytes (q3). (3) "Each implementor specifies the precise effect ... upon the alignment and representation" - the determination is docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-205 (two's complement, big-endian, the 1-2-4-8-16 ladder, NO alignment padding since WiseOwl COBOL performs no SYNCHRONIZED physical padding), which is the A.1 item 205 the rule requires (verified in the spec's own A.1: "205) USAGE BINARY clause (computer storage allocation, alignment and representation of data) ... (13.18.60, USAGE clause, General rule 4)"). conformance:cases/13.18.60-USAGE/l1_usage_binary_storage derives every expectation from GR4's own closing sentence - its header works the width floor out digit count by digit count and calls the S9(19) leg "the one that fails on the common 8-bytes-for-everything-from-10-digits-up shortcut" - so the row is closed by a spec-derived witness, not by a characterization. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/Model/PicInfo.cs#PicInfo.ByteForm (Usage.Binary -> NumericByteForm.Binary); src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/Model/PicInfo.cs#PicInfo.StorageWidth (the 1-2-4-8-16 digit ladder); src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/Model/DataItem.cs#DataItem.ElementaryByteWidth; src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/Values/Numeric/CobolNum.Image.cs; docs/CONFORMANCE.md#DOC-A.1-205 || editions, verbatim from the adjudication: 85,2002,2014,2023 (USAGE BINARY is a COBOL-85 element; probe q63 compiles `PIC S9(4) BINARY` at --std 85 and displays 1234)
